basis_key.settled: Jeremy has decided it (work order 009, 'Settled after the first draft', 22 October 2026); where the GDD records it, the line is quoted
basis_key.derived: follows from a quoted GDD line or an existing approved file; the derivation names it
basis_key.proposal: a choice made here for Jeremy to accept or change; not canon
basis_key.open: the model needs it but neither the GDD nor a derivation gives it; value is null and the work order that will set it is named

units.settled: Work order 009: 'Hit points and damage are scaled x10, so the engine rolls whole numbers.'
units.rule: Every hit point and damage quantity (max HP, monster HP, max hits, swing damage, DPS, Ration heal) is ten times its revision-1 value. Times, probabilities, multipliers, levels, accuracy, evasion and armour are not HP or damage and are unchanged. Every kill time, Ration count per kill, damage share and win chance is a ratio of two scaled quantities, so all are unchanged from revision 1.
units.whole_number_rolls: The engine rolls whole numbers of damage; how it rounds is the engine's own concern, not part of this model. Checks use the closed forms below as written, with continuous moments. At x10 scale rounding a roll moves a swing's mean by at most 0.5 HP.

closed_forms_for_checks.settled: Work order 009, settled with revision 2: 'Checks use the closed forms as written (continuous moments); the engine's whole-number rolls are its own concern.'

PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S.note: One swing every 3 s for every style and weapon. Weapons do not carry their own interval, to keep gear to two numbers.

BETWEEN_KILLS_S.note: Time from one kill to the next fight starting. About 11% of the shortest seconds_per_kill (54 s, Rust Rat Runt).

KNOCKOUT_RESPAWN_S.gdd: Section 1: 'a knockout (60-second respawn, then the queue resumes)'; section 6: 'A knockout respawns in 60 seconds and resumes the queue'.

REFERENCE_RATION_TRIGGER_HP_FRACTION.gdd: Section 6: 'triggers ("eat a Ration below 40% HP")'; section 7, first session step 5, the same trigger. The player may set others; 0.4 is the reference.

HP_BASE.note: Revision 1's 90, scaled x10 (units.HP_DAMAGE_SCALE, settled). The base value itself is still a proposal.

HP_PER_VITALITY.note: Revision 1's 10, scaled x10. Vitality 1 gives 1,000 HP.

DAMAGE_PER_STYLE_LEVEL.note: Each style level adds this to the max hit before multipliers. Revision 1 added the style level itself (1 per level); x10 scaling makes it 10. weapon.power is stated in the same scaled units.

PRESSURE_DAMAGE_PER_LEVEL.note: +1% max hit per Pressure level, every style. A multiplier, so unscaled.

HIT_CHANCE_BASE.note: Player hit chance when accuracy equals the monster's evasion.

ARMOUR_HALF_POINT.note: Revision 17 (work order 037, decision 9, Jeremy, 3 November 2026: 'The first armour does visibly more'): 100 to 25, so the first piece (Silk Hand-Wraps, 3.19 armour, on Fortitude 1) moves a hit from 96% to 86% of its strength (was 99% to 96%); every monster's max_hit was rescaled by mult_100(A_ref) / mult_25(A_ref) at its own reference armour A_ref, so every reference kill time, damage share, Ration use and boss win chance is unchanged (see revision_17_change). Armour 25 halves damage taken. Armour is Fortitude level plus the armour points of every worn Head, Body, Hands, Feet and Off-hand piece (revision 10; revision 9 had one armour piece), not HP, so it is not scaled.
ARMOUR_HALF_POINT.revision_17_basis: proposal (the draftsman, 3 November 2026) for Jeremy, under decision 9
ARMOUR_HALF_POINT.revision_17_change: constants.ARMOUR_HALF_POINT 100 to 25. Every monster/2 max_hit x mult_100(A_ref) / mult_25(A_ref), mult_H(A) = H / (A + H), A_ref the reference player's armour against that monster as check_combat.py builds it, rounded to a whole number: Runt 47 to 64 (A_ref 13.75), Scrounger 52 to 79 (20.75), Tinplate 64 to 106 (27.63), Gaffer 71 to 124 (33.31), Scrapjaw 649 to 1096 (29.81), Soot Wraith Wisp 72 to 117 (26.25), Drifter 81 to 155 (43.88), Billow 90 to 179 (49.19), Overman 99 to 204 (55.06), Old Bellows 804 to 1553 (45.06). The reference player's damage per swing is unchanged (to rounding), so every kill time, damage share, Ration use and boss win chance at the reference is unchanged: the combat check reads every non-boss at +0.0% and Scrapjaw 0.500, Old Bellows 0.501.
ARMOUR_HALF_POINT.revision_17_why: No armour piece changes (gear.slot_rules' armour rules are untouched); the Charm's rule moved with it afterwards, to keep equal value (gear.equal_value.charm_change). At 100 a level-1 piece moved a hit from 99% to 96% of its strength, which 6 of 8 playtest reads called useless (first-day-plan.md, Ledger). At 25 the Silk Hand-Wraps on Fortitude 1 move it from 96% to 86%, and on Fortitude 3, where a player stands when sitting 2 asks for them, from 89% to 80%. The lever was chosen over raising ARMOUR_FLOOR (about 10 for the same effect), which would change every one of the 66 armour pieces and flatten the slope between tiers.
ARMOUR_HALF_POINT.revision_17_consequences: Armour and Fortitude now weigh four times as much against a monster's max hit. A Tinker below the reference takes more than before: naked at level 1 a Runt's hit lands at 96% of 64 (61.5) against 99% of 47 (46.5), +32%; in the assayer's walk the first night, fought bare, eats 149 of the starter crate's 342 Rations against 116 (+28%), and the crate still covers it; later the walk, which lags the reference set, buys Rations at the same sittings as before. A Tinker above it takes less. Restated after Jeremy accepted 25 (decision 13, 3 November 2026): gear.full_set_at_reference, gear.armour_floor's percentages, gear.equal_value (at 25 equal value needs x = 37.5 a / (A + 25), so the Charm rose to 3.25 + L / 20 and seven monsters' hp rose with it, gear.equal_value.charm_change), and combat_xp_split's Fortitude figures.

WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER.note: A matched style's max hit is multiplied by this. The band consequence of 1.25 under a one-style player is settled (see weakness); the value itself rests on that acceptance.

REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL.note: A reference player loses a quarter of their HP per at-level kill. Without Rations that is a knockout about every 4 kills.

BOSS_TARGET_WIN_CHANCE.gdd: Section 7: 'she beats Scrapjaw on her second attempt'. With win chance P, expected attempts to the first win are 1/P; 1/P = 2 gives P = 0.5.

BOSS_RATION_CAP_PER_ATTEMPT.gdd: Section 6: 'A boss fight allows at most 3 Rations.'

MAIN_COMBAT_SKILL_SHARE.gdd: content/tuning/xp-curve.json assumptions.MAIN_COMBAT_SKILL_SHARE. Which skill takes it is settled (combat_xp_split).

RATION_HEAL_HP.settled: Work order 012, 'Settled after review' (22 October 2026): 'The Ration heal is settled at 600.'
RATION_HEAL_HP.note: Settled in revision 6. Work order 012 (revision 5) kept 600 as the heal of the Rustmoor Ration, the only Ration item; it was provisional in revisions 1 to 4 (work order 009: 'How much a Ration heals is for the Cooking work order, within the model's rules'). No monster changes. x10 units. Chosen within rations.needs for the reference player at levels 1 to 20 against Rustmoor-level monsters: the hard rule (heal > reference monster_dps * PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S) needs more than 15.6, set by the Rust Rat Runt (0.25 * 1000 / 48 * 3); the soft rule (heal <= (1 - REFERENCE_RATION_TRIGGER_HP_FRACTION) * max_hp) allows at most 600, set by the smallest reference max HP in the band (1000 at level 1). 600 is the largest heal that never overheals at the 40% trigger anywhere in the band.

CALIBRATION_STEP.note: How much one calibration level raises a gear stat. Left to the calibration work order (work order 009, 'Settled after the first draft': 'The calibration step is left to the calibration work order').

skills._note: Section 6, Skills table: Vitality 'Hit points'; Pressure 'Steam-driven force'; Precision 'Accuracy and crits'; Melee 'Close damage'; Marksmanship 'Ranged damage'; Aetherics 'Storm and steam magic'; Fortitude 'Defence'. Which skill feeds which stat is derived from that table; every formula and coefficient is a proposal.

precision.formula: adds precision to accuracy; crit_chance = min(CRIT_CHANCE_CAP, CRIT_CHANCE_PER_PRECISION * precision)

melee.stat: style level when the weapon's style is melee

marksmanship.stat: style level when the weapon's style is marksmanship

aetherics.stat: style level when the weapon's style is aetherics

fortitude.formula: armour = fortitude + head.armour + body.armour + hands.armour + feet.armour + off_hand.armour (an empty slot gives 0); damage_taken_mult = 1 - armour / (armour + ARMOUR_HALF_POINT)
fortitude.basis: proposal; the seven slots are settled (gear.loadout); Off-hand giving armour is a proposal (gear.slot_rules.off_hand)
fortitude.no_longer_a_gate: Fortitude no longer decides which armour a Tinker can wear; combat level does (gear.combat_level, settled 30 October 2026). Fortitude still adds its level to armour.

skills.styles_are_symmetric: The three style skills use identical formulas; they differ only through weapons and monster weakness. Derived from section 6: 'no skill is cheaper to level than another' read together with 'loadouts matter'; the symmetry itself is a proposal.

player_formulas.accuracy: style_level + precision + weapon.accuracy + charm.accuracy (an empty Charm slot gives 0; revision 10, gear.slot_rules.charm)
player_formulas.armour: fortitude + head.armour + body.armour + hands.armour + feet.armour + off_hand.armour (skills.fortitude; revision 10)
player_formulas.max_hit: (weapon.power + DAMAGE_PER_STYLE_LEVEL * style_level) * pressure_mult * (WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER if weapon.style == monster.weakness else 1)
player_formulas.landed_hit_roll: modelled as uniform on [0, max_hit]; a crit multiplies the roll by CRIT_MULTIPLIER. The engine rolls whole numbers (units.whole_number_rolls)

gear._note: Shape only. Section 6: 'Gear has fixed stats per calibration level, so a +5 Brass Spanner is identical everywhere'; section 6 Skills table: 'Calibrating ... Gear +1 to +20'. Values come in work order 011.

loadout.rule: A loadout fills seven slots, one piece in each, and any slot may be empty (an empty slot gives 0 of its stat). Its focus is the weapon's style. Consumables (Rations, teas) are not loadout slots; they are set by triggers. Tools are not combat slots: each gathering and production skill has its own tool slot (content/tuning/tools.json).

consumables.settled: Work order 009, settled with revision 2: 'Consumables are set by triggers, not loadout slots. GDD section 7's calming tea is a trigger.'

loadout.settled: Jeremy, 30 October 2026 (work order 029, 'Settled before you start'): 'Seven combat slots: Weapon, Off-hand, Head, Body, Hands, Feet, Charm. One piece in each.'
loadout.gdd: Section 6, Combat: 'A loadout fills seven gear slots, Weapon, Off-hand, Head, Body, Hands, Feet and a Charm, and its focus is the weapon's style: Melee, Marksmanship or Aetherics.'
loadout.replaces: Revision 9's two slots, ['weapon', 'armour'] (work order 009, 'Gear slots for the capstone: one weapon and one armour piece').

combat_level.rule: combat_level = max(melee, marksmanship, aetherics). Head, Body, Hands, Feet, Off-hand and Charm are worn when combat_level >= level_required. A weapon is still wielded when its style's level >= level_required (gear.weapon).
combat_level.settled: Work order 029, 'Settled before you start': 'armour, Off-hand and Charm by combat level, the highest of Melee, Marksmanship and Aetherics'.
combat_level.gdd: Section 6, Combat: 'Armour is worn by combat level, the Tinker's highest attack style, so it keeps pace with weapons'; Gear and tools: 'Weapons are wielded by their style's level, armour by combat level, and tools by their own skill's level.'
combat_level.reference: derived: the reference player's main style is at L and the other two styles at secondary_level(L) <= L (reference_player), so the reference combat level is L, the main level. Revision 9 gated armour on Fortitude, which is secondary_level(L): 6 at main level 20, 10 at 45.

slot_rules._note: What each slot gives at +0. Every rule uses a stat the model already has (armour points, accuracy). Rows +1 to +20 stay null until CALIBRATION_STEP is set, as for weapons. The derivations are in armour_share, armour_floor and equal_value.

head.basis: that it gives armour is settled (work order 029 scope 1); the floor is settled (Jeremy, 30 October 2026 (work order 029)) and its value 3 a proposal (armour_floor); the slope is derived (armour_share)

off_hand.rule: armour(0) = 3 + 3 * level_required / 16, the same as one body piece, floor included
off_hand.basis: proposal (standing default, not objected to); a guard held in the free hand, its size from equal_value. It adds to the four pieces' set, it does not take a share of it.

weapons.rule: No weapon blocks the Off-hand; every weapon is one-handed for the model.
weapons.basis: proposal (the orchestrator, 30 October 2026), for the weapons work orders to revisit (a rifle or a two-handed hammer may).

charm.basis: proposal (standing default, not objected to) for the stat and the slope (equal_value; 1 / 20 at both half-points); the floor 3.25 a proposal (the draftsman, 3 November 2026, under decision 13), re-derived from equal_value at ARMOUR_HALF_POINT 25
charm.floor_basis: proposal. Revision 17: 3.25 is the least-squares line through equal_value's x = 37.5 a / (A + 25) at combat levels 1 to 45 (3.265 + 0.0500 L), its floor rounded to a quarter; 3.09 at L 1. Before revision 17: 1, an extension of Jeremy's floor rule by the orchestrator, 30 October 2026, what equal_value gave a level-1 piece at ARMOUR_HALF_POINT 100 (37.5 x 3.19 / 113.75 = 1.05).

slot_rules.level_required: combat level for head, body, hands, feet, off_hand and charm (combat_level); style level for the weapon

armour_share.rule: Above the floor, the four armour slots share a zone's armour equally: the sloped part of a full four-piece set at combat level C is 4 * 3C/16 = 3C/4 armour points, and each piece is a quarter of it, so no slot dominates.
armour_share.derivation: derived. Work order 028 settled armour(0) = 3 x the Fortitude level required, for one piece. Work order 029 asks for it restated against combat level, with the reference player's combat level in place of Fortitude. The reference player at combat level C has Fortitude secondary_level(C): 6 at 20, 10 at 45, 18 at 70 (reference_player). A least-squares line through the origin on those three checkpoints gives Fortitude = 0.2498 C, so Fortitude is about C / 4 and the settled piece is worth 3 x C / 4 at combat level C. The four pieces share that; each slopes at 3C/16. At the checkpoints the sloped part gives 15, 33.75 and 52.5 points against the settled 18, 30 and 54 (-17%, +12.5%, -3%).
armour_share.equal_shares: proposal (standing default, not objected to). GDD section 6 names the four slots and gives no reason one should outweigh another.

armour_floor.rule: ARMOUR_FLOOR = 3 armour points on every Head, Body, Hands, Feet and Off-hand piece at +0, added to its level-based share.
armour_floor.settled: Jeremy, 30 October 2026 (work order 029): 'Every piece gets a floor. Each Head, Body, Hands, Feet and Off-hand piece gets a base armour value plus its level-based share, so a first Rustmoor set noticeably cuts Rations eaten.'
armour_floor.derivation: proposal for the value 3, derived as follows. The floor is the settled rule's own level-1 piece: work order 028's 3 x level_required at level 1 is 3, so no piece is ever worth less than the smallest piece Jeremy settled. What reads as felt comes from work order 028's settlement: the draft's 1x rule, which cut damage 5 to 8%, was rejected, and the 3x rule, cutting about 15%, was accepted. At 3 the five armour pieces of a level-1 set are 15.94 armour on top of Fortitude 1, which alone cuts Rations eaten against the Rust Rat Runt from 0.416 to 0.358 a kill, -13.9%: clear of the rejected band and near the accepted 15%. With the Charm's proposed floor of 1 as well, the full set's cut is -16.3% (0.348 a kill; full_set_at_reference). Armour-only floors of 2, 3.5 and 4 would give -10.1%, -15.9% and -17.5%. Those figures were against ARMOUR_HALF_POINT 100 and the one-weapon monsters of revision 9. Restated at 25 (revision 17) against today's Runt (max_hit 64), the same five floor-3 pieces on Fortitude 1 cut Rations per kill from 0.600 to 0.372, -38.0% (full_set_at_reference); armour-only floors of 2, 3.5 and 4 would give -29.7%, -41.5% and -44.7%. The floor stays 3: decision 13 chose the half-point as the lever and left every piece's points alone (constants.ARMOUR_HALF_POINT.revision_17_why).
armour_floor.later_levels: The floor is flat, so it matters most early: a level-20 piece is 3 + 3.75 = 6.75, and a full level-20 set (five pieces) is 33.75 points against 18.75 without it.
armour_floor.basis: settled for the floor (Jeremy, 30 October 2026 (work order 029)); the value 3 is a proposal

equal_value.rule: Off-hand and Charm were each sized to be worth one armour piece to the reference player at their level_required, so removing any one of the six non-weapon pieces raises damage taken per kill by about the same share.
equal_value.off_hand: Giving it the same armour as one piece, floor included, meets the rule exactly.
equal_value.charm: Derived. Damage taken per kill scales as 1 / hit_chance through the unfloored fight time and as (A + H) / (A + a + H) through armour, H = ARMOUR_HALF_POINT. With hit chance at HIT_CHANCE_BASE (0.75), x accuracy matches one piece a against the other armour A when x = 37.5 a / (A + H). Revision 17 (H 25): with a = 3 + 3L/16 and A = Fortitude secondary_level(L) + 4a, x is 3.09 at L 1, 3.45 at 5, 3.77 at 10, 4.09 at 15, 4.36 at 20, 4.67 at 25, 4.86 at 30, 5.03 at 35, 5.31 at 45; the least-squares line over L 1 to 45 is 3.265 + 0.0500 L, so the rule is 3.25 + L / 20 (slot_rules.charm), within -3.6% to +7.0% of x over L 1 to 45. Checked against the combat check's own reference ladder: removing one armour piece raises damage per kill by 8.9%, 9.9%, 10.8% at the Scrounger, Tinplate and Gaffer and 12.4%, 12.8%, 13.3% at the Drifter, Billow and Overman; removing the Charm, by 9.2%, 9.9%, 10.5% and 11.9%, 12.5%, 12.9%. At 1 + L / 20 the Charm gave 3.2% to 6.9%, about half a piece. Above L 45 the line runs ahead of x (6.75 against 5.63 at L 70), for the Thunderhead's gear work order to revisit. Before revision 17 (H 100): x = 1.16 at L 20, 2.20 at 45, 2.89 at 70 without the floor, fitted as 0.0443 L and rounded to L / 20, and with the floor about 1 + L / 20.
equal_value.charm_change: Revision 17, applied with decision 13: every Charm's +0 accuracy rises by 2.25 (16 pieces, content/gear/rustmoor-pieces.json and cinderworks-pieces.json). A larger Charm speeds the reference player's kills, so each monster whose reference wears a Charm has its hp scaled by the reference's mean-swing ratio new / old (hit chance 0.75 + 0.02 (acc - evasion), the only term that moves), which keeps t_pure, damage per kill, Rations, kill time and boss win chance at the reference, then set to the whole number nearest the exact solve of seconds_per_kill (hp x (seconds_per_kill - 6) / (computed - 6)): Scrounger 1664 to 1760 (x 1.05814 gives 1760.7; the exact solve 1759.99, since 1664 sat 0.06 s over its target), Tinplate 5263 to 5567 (1.05777), Gaffer 10849 to 11471 (1.05740; exact 11471.4), Scrapjaw 13272 to 14044 (1.05814; boss.reference_weapon pieces_derivation), Drifter 28132 to 29726 (1.05668), Billow 40232 to 42498 (1.05632), Overman 54613 to 57678 (1.05611; exact 57677.6). The Runt, Wisp and Old Bellows' references wear no Charm and are unchanged. With the Charm alone the check failed seven targets (kill time -5.2% to -5.7%, Scrapjaw 0.593); with the rescale every non-boss reads +0.0%, Scrapjaw 0.500, Old Bellows 0.501. A Tinker without a Charm now kills those seven about 5.7% slower than before; one with the zone's Charm, as before.

The engine and the combat check still read them that way. No new gear is drafted on slot 'armour'.
legacy_armour_slot.consequence: Moved under this revision's rule, a level-20 piece gives 6.75 armour where the Gauze Goggles give 18 today; the move re-rates them.
legacy_armour_slot.retired: Revision 16 (work order 034, Part 1): no gear entry uses the 'armour' slot. The five pieces it held are gear/2 pieces in content/gear/cinderworks-pieces.json under gear.slot_rules: the Gauze Goggles, Furnace Goggles and Founder's Goggles in head at combat levels 20, 30 and 40, the Slag Wool Coat and Studded Felt Coat in body at 20 and 25. The slot stays in gear/2's enum and the checks until the toolwright removes it.

reference_gear.rule: For the target, 'the gear the zone offers' is the best +0 weapon of the matched style with level_required at or below the main style level, and in each of off_hand, head, body, hands, feet and charm the best +0 piece the zone offers with level_required at or below the reference combat level (the main level L; combat_level.reference). A slot the zone fills with nothing below L is empty and gives 0. Calibration is headroom above the target, not part of it (section 7 month three treats calibrating toward +10 as a long sink); it is what earns kill_time.floor's cap. Bosses are the exception: a boss's weapon is boss.reference_weapon where listed, and its six non-weapon slots are what work order 025's Act I walk actually holds before the fight (boss.reference_weapon._non_weapon_slots). A boss's own drops never count for it (as the combat check reads it). kill_time.floor's T_ref is a different reference: it draws on every zone at the player's own levels.

weakness.rule: A weapon whose style equals monster.weakness multiplies max_hit by WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER. Unmatched weapons take no penalty beyond missing the bonus.
weakness.consequence: With Rations stocked, computed fight time scales inversely with the player's DPS, so the reference player's unmatched computed seconds per kill = BETWEEN_KILLS_S + WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER * (seconds_per_kill - BETWEEN_KILLS_S). Tinplate: 162 s matched, 201 s unmatched. The kill-time floor does not bind on an unmatched at-level fight, since it is already slower than seconds_per_kill.

kill_time._note: Closed form, expected values, no simulation. seconds_per_kill in the monster files is the full cycle used by the pacing check (xp / seconds_per_kill), so it includes the time between kills and eating. Every HP and damage quantity below is in x10 units; every time is in seconds and unchanged by the scale.
kill_time.ration_drag: f = monster_dps * PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S / ration.heal_hp  (eating costs one player swing while the monster keeps attacking); requires f < 1

unstocked.assumptions: No HP regeneration between kills; a knockout restores full HP after the respawn; the half-fought monster is lost, costing on average half a fight (an approximation).

floor.formula: expected_seconds_per_kill = max(T_own, monster.seconds_per_kill * max(KILL_TIME_CAP_FRACTION, min(1, gear_ratio))), with gear_ratio = T_own / T_ref, at every player level, for every non-boss monster

gear_ratio.T_own: computed_seconds_per_kill (kill_time.stocked: BETWEEN_KILLS_S + t_pure / (1 - f)) for the player exactly as they fight: their seven combat skill levels, the gear they wear in all seven slots at its calibration, their buffs and consumables, Rations stocked, against this monster.
gear_ratio.T_ref: min over the three styles s in {melee, marksmanship, aetherics} of computed_seconds_per_kill for the same player, with the same seven skill levels and the same buffs and consumables, Rations stocked, against the same monster, wearing reference loadout s: (1) weapon: the +0 weapon of style s with level_required <= the player's level in s that gives the highest mean swing against this monster, ties to the lower item id (the style level in max_hit and accuracy is the player's level in s, and WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER applies when s is the monster's weakness); (2) each of off_hand, head, body, hands and feet: the +0 piece with the most armour, and charm: the +0 piece with the most accuracy, each with level_required <= the player's combat level, ties to the lower item id, empty (0) when none qualifies. A style with no qualifying weapon is left out of the minimum. Only the six slots of gear.loadout count; the legacy 'armour' slot does not.
gear_ratio.pool: Reference pieces for T_ref come from every zone's gear files, at or below the player's own levels, boss drops included, never from the monster's zone alone. Boss drops count like any other piece (proposal). Scrapjaw's Cleaver (melee, level 20, +0 power 180) earns nothing because it is in the pool itself: Rustmoor has no other level-20 melee weapon, so at Melee 20 the Cleaver is T_ref's melee weapon, and wielding it gives gear_ratio 1.
gear_ratio.pool_basis: settled, Jeremy, 30 October 2026 (work order 029): only being ahead of your own level counts, so bringing later-zone gear back to an earlier zone does not earn the cap.
gear_ratio.fastest_style_basis: proposal (the orchestrator's correction after the inspector's review, 30 October 2026): taking the fastest of the three styles means levels alone, or an off-style matchup, never earn the cap.
gear_ratio.reference_player: derived: the reference player at monster level L has main style L in the monster's weakness and the other styles at secondary_level(L) < L, so the fastest of the three reference loadouts is the main style's, which is the gear it wears (gear.reference_gear; +0 stats follow level-only rules, so the all-zone pool gives the same pieces wherever the zone has a piece at that level). T_own = T_ref, gear_ratio = 1, expected = seconds_per_kill, and the combat band stays at 13.96 days.

KILL_TIME_CAP_FRACTION.settled: Jeremy, 30 October 2026 (work order 029): 0.75 is the value. Not yet a constant: tuning.combat/1 allows no new constant, so it sits here until the toolwright adds it to the schema and check_combat.py.

floor.basis: settled for the principle, the cap value, the boss exclusion and the all-zone pool (Jeremy, 30 October 2026); the fastest-style minimum and boss drops counting are proposals
floor.gdd: Section 6: 'A Tinker who outlevels a monster still takes its usual time per kill, so fighting easy monsters is safe but no faster; the reward for levelling is reaching harder ones.' Amended by work order 029 (30 October 2026): levels alone still buy no speed, but gear better than the reference for the Tinker's own level may beat seconds_per_kill, down to KILL_TIME_CAP_FRACTION of it. GDD section 6 now carries it: 'better gear than a Tinker's level calls for can cut a kill to three quarters of its usual time, but never a boss fight (amended 30 October 2026)'. Work order 009, settled with revision 2: 'The kill-time floor applies at every level, not only at or above the monster's level. Nothing kills faster than its target time' is replaced by this rule.
floor.cases: Gear no better than T_ref's loadouts: gear_ratio >= 1, clamped to 1, so expected = max(T_own, seconds_per_kill): outlevelling alone is safe but no faster, as before, and levels can still make up for weak gear back to seconds_per_kill. Better gear (calibrated pieces, or a piece whose stats are ahead of its level's rule): gear_ratio < 1, so the kill time falls in proportion, to no less than KILL_TIME_CAP_FRACTION * seconds_per_kill.
floor.why_own_level: derived: measuring gear against the reference at the monster's level would let the band's own reference player beat targets. At level 18 it holds level-15 weapons and fights the level-10 Tinplate, which would then pay 30 XP per 121.5 s, 889 XP/h, against the at-level Gaffer's 700 XP/h. Easier monsters would out-pay harder ones, breaking section 6's 'the reward for levelling is reaching harder ones', and the combat band would fall to 11.30 days with Rustmoor's settled weapons (11.01 with a weapon at every level). Measured against the player's own levels, every style and every zone, the reference player always has gear_ratio 1.
floor.how_far_ahead: derived: the reference fight has seconds_per_kill = BETWEEN_KILLS_S + t_fight, and t_fight scales as 1 / mean swing, so reaching the cap needs a mean swing (seconds_per_kill - 6) / (0.75 * seconds_per_kill - 6) times T_ref's: 1.391 (Runt), 1.360 (Scrounger), 1.351 (Tinplate), 1.346 (Gaffer). By weapon power alone that is about 1.7x the 10 x level rule. Accuracy alone cannot reach it, since a 1.35x hit chance passes HIT_CHANCE_MAX. T_ref already holds the best +0 piece the player can wear in every slot, from every zone, boss drops included, so no +0 piece can be ahead of it: the Cleaver, for one, is T_ref's own melee weapon at Melee 20 (gear_ratio.pool). The cap is earned only by Calibrating, or by gear genuinely ahead of the player's level. A smaller lead buys a proportional saving.
floor.legacy_armour: Legacy Fortitude-gated armour (the five Cinderworks pieces on slot 'armour', gear.legacy_armour_slot) counts in T_own when worn but never in T_ref, whose loadouts fill only the six gear.loadout slots. A Tinker wearing one is a little faster than T_ref, about 0.1% against today's Rustmoor rats. The gap closes when the Cinderworks armour moves into the new slots, before the Soot Wraiths work order. The engine makes the same choice as the check.

kill_time.target: For the reference player at monster.level with a matched reference_gear loadout and Rations stocked, computed_seconds_per_kill == monster.seconds_per_kill and monster_dps * t_fight == REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL * max_hp.
kill_time.solving_for_011: Pick evasion (suggested: equal to the reference accuracy, so the reference hit chance is HIT_CHANCE_BASE), hit_chance and attack_interval_s; then monster_dps = REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL * max_hp / (seconds_per_kill - BETWEEN_KILLS_S) fixes max_hit, and hp = player_dps * (seconds_per_kill - BETWEEN_KILLS_S) * (1 - f) fixes hp, rounded to a whole number.

rations._note: Section 6 ('eat a Ration below 40% HP') and the Skills table (Cooking produces 'Healing rations') name Rations. Since revision 5 one Ration item exists, item.rustmoor.rustmoor_ration (work order 012), healing RATION_HEAL_HP. Below is what the model needs from any Ration.

needs.heal_hp: a fixed whole number per Ration item, in x10 units (work order 009, 'Settled after the first draft': 'How much a Ration heals is for the Cooking work order, within the model's rules'). Settled at 600 for the Rustmoor Ration (constants.RATION_HEAL_HP; work order 012, 'Settled after review': 'The Ration heal is settled at 600.'): it meets hard_rule against every Rustmoor monster and is the largest heal that meets soft_rule at every reference level 1 to 20.
needs.hard_rule: heal_hp > monster_dps * PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S for any monster it is meant for, or the stocked formula diverges
needs.soft_rule: heal_hp <= (1 - REFERENCE_RATION_TRIGGER_HP_FRACTION) * max_hp of the reference player at the Ration's tier, so eating at the trigger never overheals
needs.consumption: rations_per_kill = monster_dps * t_fight / heal_hp (kill_time.stocked.rations_per_kill); at the reference, where kill_time.target gives monster_dps * t_fight == REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL * max_hp, that is REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL * max_hp / heal_hp, with no further division by (1 - f). This is Cooking's demand per kill
needs.boss_cap: At most BOSS_RATION_CAP_PER_ATTEMPT (3) per boss attempt (settled).

rations.reference_use: At the reference with heal 600, from kill_time.stocked.rations_per_kill as the combat and drops checks compute it (drops check, Crown sink report, revision 7): 0.416, 0.458, 0.542, 0.583 Rations per kill and 27.72, 15.28, 12.04, 9.72 Rations an hour against the Runt, Scrounger, Tinplate and Gaffer; 2,085 Rations over the 1 to 20 band.

It now agrees with kill_time.stocked.rations_per_kill, the formula the combat and drops checks use. reference_use was computed with the old formula (0.428, 0.465, 0.547, 0.588 a kill; 28.5, 15.5, 12.2, 9.8 an hour; 2,110 over the band) and is restated. No constant, monster or check result changes.
rations.basis: proposal for the rules (work order 012); heal_hp settled at 600 (work order 012, 'Settled after review'); boss cap settled

boss._note: Section 6: 'a boss attempt is a separate queue item, and a lost fight spends the attempt and pays no XP'. A boss fight is a race between two times, each approximated as normal (renewal central limit), so win chance is closed form.
boss.player_time: m_p = PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S * boss.hp / mean_swing_damage + n * PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S, where n = BOSS_RATION_CAP_PER_ATTEMPT if Rations are stocked else 0 (assumes every allowed Ration is eaten)
boss.player_time_variance: v_p = PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S^2 * boss.hp * var_swing / mean_swing_damage^3, var_swing = second_moment - mean^2
boss.boss_time: m_b = boss.attack_interval_s * pool / boss_mean_swing, pool = max_hp + n * ration.heal_hp
boss.win_chance: P = Phi((m_b - m_p) / sqrt(v_p + v_b)), Phi the standard normal CDF. Every term in the ratio is a time, so the x10 scale leaves P unchanged.
boss.target: For the reference player at boss.level with a matched loadout and n Rations, m_b == m_p (so P == BOSS_TARGET_WIN_CHANCE) and BETWEEN_KILLS_S + m_p == boss.seconds_per_kill.

combat_xp_split.rule: Each kill's combat XP goes MAIN_COMBAT_SKILL_SHARE (70%) to the loadout's focus, which is the style skill of the weapon (Melee, Marksmanship or Aetherics), and OTHER_COMBAT_SKILLS_SHARE_EACH (5%) to each of the other six combat skills. Vitality, Fortitude, Pressure and Precision can never be the focus and always take the 5% share.
combat_xp_split.gdd: Section 6: 'its focus is the weapon's style: Melee, Marksmanship or Aetherics'; work order 009: 'Only the three attack styles can be a loadout's focus. Vitality, Fortitude, Pressure and Precision always take the 5% share.'
combat_xp_split.why: The curve's base, its day-2 check (total level passes 50 only at 70/5 with three crafting skills) and the Ledger Page counter (work order 008) all rest on 70/5.
consequences: Vitality and Fortitude sit at 6, 10 and 18 when the main skill reaches 20, 45 and 70 (reference_player table): max HP 1,500, 1,900, 2,700; damage taken cut by 19.4%, 28.6%, 41.9% by Fortitude alone (f / (f + ARMOUR_HALF_POINT), revision 17; 5.7%, 9.1%, 15.3% at 100).

Vitality and Fortitude do not change at-level kill time. They change Ration use, knockouts without Rations, and boss odds: at Scrapjaw (melee reference player, Riveting Hammer, the walk's six pieces, boss.reference_weapon; 3 Rations, RATION_HEAL_HP 600; revision 17), +5 Vitality (max HP 1,500 to 2,000) takes the win chance from 50% to 74%, +5 Fortitude (armour 29.81 to 34.81) to 65%. Before revision 17 (ARMOUR_HALF_POINT 100, no pieces): 73% and 58% (armour 6 to 11).
A player who switches styles to match every weakness splits the 70% across up to three styles and levels each more slowly than the curve assumes.
Story checks on Vitality, Fortitude, Pressure or Precision cannot assume more than about 6 in Act I, 10 in Act II, 18 in Act III.
